walkthroughs.body_html:
On the Wild Side — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

On the Wild Side brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with On the Wild Side.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why are frameshift mutations usually more severe than point substitutions?
options: Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.
Frameshifts only change the codon at the site of the mutation, like a substitution.
Insertions/deletions of a non-multiple of 3 shift the reading frame, changing every codon downstream of the mutation.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.
It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2 in humans.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.
Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.
